role: the machine operator who has lost work
verdict: No: the spec makes the promotion commit crash-safe and tests it, but the machine that guards work (generation, salvage, rm, recreate, retire) has no crash rule and no kill test, reads one empty sbx listing as a lost sandbox, sits behind the widening gates, and promises "nothing sandbox-only is lost" without saying what that covers, so the largest gap is that the objective's last line is neither scoped nor proven under a kill.

findings.defect: The generation machine states no persistence order and no recovery for a kill between its side effects (salvage refs per repo, the salvage record, sbx env rm, closed-removed), unlike the promotion commit, which has both.
findings.scenario: romeu rm completes a salvage, records result complete, runs sbx env rm, and is killed before writing closed-removed; the next run finds the generation salvaging with the sandbox absent and applies the crash-recovery row, closing it as closed-lost with a new result lost record, so history says lost when nothing was; a kill between the create-only refs of the first repo and the second leaves a record whose refsPrefix covers half the repos, with no rule saying what the next command does.
findings.change: Add to 01 1.6 a step list for the destructive commands, written like the promotion commit: (1) write the salvage record with state pending and its id; (2) create the refs per repo; (3) mark the record complete or incomplete; (4) write removing before sbx env rm; (5) sbx env rm; (6) closed-removed. Then add one recovery rule per intermediate state, for example "removing and the sandbox absent becomes closed-removed and keeps the existing record; a pending record whose refs are partial is re-verified and finished".
findings.cost: About 20 lines in 01 1.6, two new state values in 03 3.8, and the T034 table rows.

findings.defect: I17 and 10 10.1 inject faults into the promotion commit only; no test kills romeu after each step of salvage, rm, recreate or retire, so "holds under a kill at any line" is unmeasured for the machine that protects work.
findings.scenario: An implementation writes closed-removed before sbx env rm; a kill between the two leaves a live sandbox that romeu no longer recognizes, and every CI level stays green because no test interrupts rm.
findings.change: Add to I17's Test cell and to the Additional required tests of 10 10.1 a row named "Destructive-command fault injection": a test hook kills romeu after each step of the 01 1.6 list of L4-1, for salvage, rm, recreate and retire, then asserts that the next run, salvage or rm converges, that no salvage record says lost when the record before it was complete, and that sbx env rm is never reached without a complete or accepted record of this generation.
findings.cost: A test seam and one e2e table; the fake sbx needs a mid-session kill session.

findings.defect: One sbx ls --json that does not list the sandbox is read as absent, and run then closes the generation as lost and creates a same-name sandbox with no confirmation; there is no unknown state distinct from absent.
findings.scenario: The sbx daemon is restarting, or an sbx upgrade has moved its state store, and ls returns an empty list while the old VM still exists under the project's name; romeu run (J10 step 2) records closed-lost and calls sbx env run -d, and the create step, owned by sbx, now decides the fate of a week of dirty work on negative evidence.
findings.change: In 01 1.6 and 04 4.2 run step 2: absent requires sbx ls --json to exit 0, to parse, and to report the sandbox missing on two reads a fixed interval apart; any other answer is unknown, which exits 1 with a new error id and does nothing; on a TTY, run asks before closed-lost plus create, and without a TTY it preserves and closes but does not create, so a second command is needed.
findings.cost: One state, one error id, one prompt, and a probe of ls during a daemon restart (L4-27).

findings.defect: salvage, the protective command, refuses on drift and on a gate 1 mismatch, although it widens nothing, so an sbx or romeu upgrade or a hand edit stands between the operator and the rescue of their work.
findings.scenario: sbx is upgraded because the sandbox misbehaves; romeu salvage exits 3 until approve --toolchain is run on a TTY, and a stray edit to sbxenv.yaml makes it exit 4 until sync --overwrite-drift renders a candidate that may itself need gate 2; meanwhile the sandbox dies. T074 asserts this behavior.
findings.change: In 01 1.5, replace "Destructive commands (salvage, rm, retire) may run when only the spec moved on, but never on drift or a failed identity check" with: "salvage, and salvage --from-host, run on drift and on a gate 1 or gate 2 mismatch after printing it, and never on a failed identity check; rm and retire keep the stricter rule for their removal half, after the salvage half has run". Adjust the I7 E list to match.
findings.cost: Two sentences in 01 1.5, one in I7, a change to T074.

findings.defect: A temporary file left in a memory dir by a julieta killed mid-write (snapshot, salvage payload, memory entry) violates the layout allowlist, and sync and run then refuse with exit 2, so the crash the J10 recovery exists for blocks the J10 recovery.
findings.scenario: The sandbox dies while the post-commit snapshot writes its temp file next to heads.bundle; the operator runs romeu run (J10 step 2), which exits 2 naming the leftover path, and is left to delete files by hand inside the one directory the spec tells them never to touch.
findings.change: In 08 8.1, fix the temp-name grammar for every memory write (for example .tmp-<ULID> in the target's own directory), state that a name of that grammar is not an allowlist violation and is never read, and that julieta setup removes leftovers older than its own start, as 13 13.4 does for the ledger; add the case to I24's test cell.
findings.cost: A short rule in 08 8.1, one row in I24, and one container test.

findings.defect: The generation table has no row for a sandbox half that failed (julieta exit 1, an exec timeout, the host disk full) as distinct from incomplete, and "open generation" in 1.3 F, 1.5 step 6, I26 and adopt is ambiguous beside the state names open and salvaging.
findings.scenario: julieta salvage times out; the generation stays salvaging with the sandbox present; romeu run's identity step reads "open generation" as state open and exits RJ-203, and romeu adopt refuses because a generation exists, so the operator is locked out of their own sandbox.
findings.change: Add the row "salvaging | the sandbox half fails | open | salvage record result incomplete, reason sandbox-half-failed; exit 1", and define once in 1.7 that "open generation" means a generation in state open or salvaging, then use that phrase in 1.3 F, 1.5 step 6, I26 and 04 4.2 adopt.
findings.cost: One table row, one vocabulary line, one reason value in 03 3.8.

findings.defect: "nothing sandbox-only is lost" has no scope, while 08 8.5 salvages only the generation's recorded repos and the agent profile's paths, and the salvage manifest has no way to say what it did not enumerate.
findings.scenario: The agent cloned a second repo into $HOME/scratch and kept a database data directory in /tmp; rm reports result complete and removes the sandbox; both are gone, and the operator had read 0.1 as a promise.
findings.change: Qualify 0.1: "nothing in the recorded repos (worktrees, local refs, stashes, ignored files within the cap) and the agent's state paths is lost; work elsewhere in the sandbox is outside salvage"; add the out-of-scope list to 08 8.5, a residual-risk row to 05 5.4, and say in 08 8.4 that a death keeps committed work only.
findings.cost: A few sentences on three pages; a decision if the maintainer wants the scope wider.

findings.defect: The mitigation of the row "Salvage proves that nothing the sandbox still holds is lost" says "a push to origin is the only copy an agent cannot take back", but ADR 0008 records that the sandbox's token can delete branches, tags and releases.
findings.scenario: An agent pushes its work, then deletes the remote branch or force-pushes a cleaned history, and resets locally; the next romeu fetch force-moves refs/romeu/origin, so the host's last view of the pushed commits is gone too, and the accepted risk was accepted on a premise ADR 0008 had already removed.
findings.change: Rewrite the mitigation cell to state that, with the operator's token (ADR 0008), a push is not a copy the agent cannot take back, and either add a create-only host ref per fetched origin head per generation (refs/romeu/origin-log/<dir>/<gen>/<sha>) or record the risk as accepted with that wording and a link to ADR 0008.
findings.cost: One cell rewritten; optionally a ref namespace in 02 2.3 and gitsafe.

findings.defect: The snapshot is one heads.bundle rewritten after every commit, and neither snapshot nor salvage (03 3.11) includes the reflog, so the snapshot follows an agent's destructive operation instead of protecting against it.
findings.scenario: The agent runs git reset --hard HEAD~3 and commits; post-commit rewrites heads.bundle without the three dropped commits; the sandbox dies, and the reflog that still held them dies with it.
findings.change: In 08 8.4, keep the last N snapshots (or import each into create-only host refs, L4-14), and add each branch's reflog tips that are not reachable from a branch to the bundle as refs/salvage-reflog/*; list the reflog in 03 3.11 refs[].
findings.cost: A retention rule and a refs class; bundle size grows a little.

findings.defect: The sandbox half writes objects and refs into the sandbox's own repositories, and no behavior is stated for a stopped sandbox or one that will not start, so a full VM disk or a broken boot leaves only --from-host, which drops every dirty tree and stash.
findings.scenario: The VM disk fills, the most common reason to give up on a sandbox; commit-tree fails with ENOSPC, julieta salvage exits 1, and the operator's only path is salvage --from-host with result lost.
findings.change: In 08 8.5 step 2, write salvage objects into a temporary object directory in the memory mount (GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY with the repo's objects as alternate) and bundle from there; in 04 4.2 salvage, state that a stopped sandbox is started for the sandbox half and stopped again, and that a start failure exits 1 naming --from-host and what it will not recover.
findings.cost: A design change to step 2, two sentences in 04 4.2, probe facts (L4-27).

findings.defect: Every salvage ref lives in a host clone that the spec calls a plain operator clone, and nothing checks that the refs a salvage record names still exist.
findings.scenario: The operator deletes and re-clones the secondary's navigation clone (02 2.6), or follows J13 step 4 after status shows nothing unpushed; three generations of salvage refs go with it, and status and doctor keep reporting result complete.
findings.change: Add a doctor check and a status line: for each salvage record, every ref under its refsPrefix exists in the clone of its repo, otherwise fail with a new error id naming the record; change J13 step 4 to "after status shows nothing unpushed and no salvage-only refs".
findings.cost: One check, one error id, one sentence in J13.

findings.defect: Snapshot and salvage bundles are thin against repos[].base, and on the host those prerequisites are held only by refs/romeu/origin, which a later fetch force-moves.
findings.scenario: The origin branch is force-pushed or deleted, romeu sync fetches and moves refs/romeu/origin, the operator's git gc prunes the old objects; the snapshot bundle of the dead sandbox no longer verifies, and 08 8.5 step 2's fallback of fetching origin first cannot bring back objects origin no longer has.
findings.change: In 03 3.6 and 02 2.3, have romeu create a create-only ref refs/romeu/base/<name>/<gen>/<dir>/<sha> for every base SHA it puts in a manifest, kept for the life of the generation and of its salvage records.
findings.cost: One ref namespace and a CreateRef call per manifest base.

findings.defect: --accept-loss on rm and recreate needs no TTY and accepts every reason at once, while every widening approval needs a TTY.
findings.scenario: A script runs romeu recreate --accept-loss to get past an over-cap build cache; that same run also accepts an unreadable source file and a missing repo, and nothing records that the operator accepted those specific items.
findings.change: In 04 4.2, make --accept-loss require a TTY and print each reason before a y/N prompt; add --accept-loss=<reason>[,<reason>] for non-TTY use, so only the named reasons are accepted; record the accepted reasons on the salvage record (03 3.8).
findings.cost: A flag form, a prompt, one record field.

findings.defect: Snapshot bundles stay in the agent-writable memory dir and reach host refs only at romeu pull (secondary) or when a lost generation is preserved, although romeu reads that directory at every sync and run.
findings.scenario: A cleanup script inside the sandbox removes memory/<dir>/snapshot/ by a wrong path; the next day the sandbox dies and J10 finds nothing to import. This is an accident, not the hostile agent of the accepted 05 5.4 row.
findings.change: In 08 8.4 and 04 4.2 (run and sync), have romeu verify and unbundle each snapshot into create-only refs refs/romeu/snapshots/<name>/<gen>/<snapshot-created>/... at every sync and run, as pull already does for the secondary.
findings.cost: A step in run and sync; ref growth, bounded by commits.

findings.defect: --stop-agents stops only the agent's processes, so pane steps, other shells and in-flight git operations keep changing the worktrees while step 2 captures them.
findings.scenario: npm run dev regenerates files and a second shell runs git rebase while salvage builds its temporary index; the captured tree mixes two states, or a mid-rebase worktree is captured with its rebase state left out.
findings.change: In 08 8.5 step 1, stop every process of the sandbox user except julieta (or freeze them), and after step 2 recheck each worktree's status and HEAD, repeating the capture once if either moved; record an in-progress rebase or merge as a skipped item (reason in-progress-operation), so it is never silently complete.
findings.cost: A step change and one skip reason.

findings.defect: Snapshots fire only on commit hooks, and when a repo-local core.hooksPath (set by common tools on install) disables them, only the agent and a live sandbox's julieta status know; after a death the host has no record of it.
findings.scenario: npm install runs husky, which sets core.hooksPath; snapshots of that repo stop for weeks; the sandbox dies, and J10 imports a snapshot three weeks old, and the operator learns it only from the loss.
findings.change: In 08 8.4, have julieta write snapshot/heads.json with a disabled marker and the time snapshots stopped, which romeu status reads from the host side without exec; add a time trigger (every setup and every SessionStart) besides the commit hooks.
findings.cost: One field in heads.json, a status line, a trigger.

findings.defect: Neither status nor doctor reports work at risk, and the newest facts handoff (dirty, stashes, ahead) is never used to tell the operator what a death or a --from-host salvage lost.
findings.scenario: J10 step 1 shows the snapshot time; the facts file on the host says dirty 14 and stashes 2; romeu run records result lost, and nothing tells the operator that 14 files and 2 stashes are gone.
findings.change: In 04 4.2 status, add per repo: unpushed commits at the last snapshot, the snapshot's age, snapshots disabled, and the newest facts' dirty and stash counts; in 08 8.5 step 5 and 01 1.6's lost rows, copy those counts into the salvage record as reasons (dirty-at-last-facts:<n>, stashes-at-last-facts:<n>); add a doctor warning past a snapshot age.
findings.cost: A status block, two reason forms, one doctor row.

findings.defect: "every state transition of a project is a single atomic write" is false for promotion, salvage and retire, which change several files, and retire makes two moves across $ROMEU_ROOT and $XDG_STATE_HOME with no recovery rule.
findings.scenario: retire moves <name>-env to .attic and is killed before moving the record to the state attic; the next sync finds a live record for a project with no tree and recreates <name>-env with empty memory dirs, beside the attic copy.
findings.change: Replace the sentence with "each record write is atomic; transitions that change more than one file follow the step lists of 01 1.6", and add a retire step list: write retiring to the record, move the tree, move the record; a record in retiring with the tree in the attic is finished by the next command.
findings.cost: A sentence and a short step list.

findings.defect: No rule says what romeu does with a host state record it cannot decode (corrupt, truncated, written by a newer or older romeu), and no migration rule for state-*.v1 exists, although that record is the only index of where salvaged work is.
findings.scenario: The operator downgrades romeu after a bad release; strict decoding refuses projects/<name>.json, every command exits 2 including salvage, and the sandbox with the week of work cannot be salvaged by the romeu at hand.
findings.change: In 03 3.8, state that romeu reads its own version and the previous one and migrates on the next write; that a record it cannot decode is reported by status and doctor with a new error id; and that salvage --from-host still runs from the tree and the clones alone, recording into a new record beside the unreadable one, which is never overwritten.
findings.cost: A rule, an error id, a read-only path.

findings.defect: Atomic writes are temp, fsync and rename without a directory fsync, memory writes (08 8.1) say temp and rename with no fsync, and the snapshot (08 8.4) only says "written atomically".
findings.scenario: A power loss right after the rename of a project record leaves the old record on disk after reboot, and the generation the operator just opened is gone from state.
findings.change: State one durability rule in 03 3.8 (write temp, fsync file, rename, fsync directory) and cite it from 08 8.1, 08 8.4 and 13 13.5.
findings.cost: One sentence and three citations.

findings.defect: When promotion recovery finds a candidate that no longer verifies, the text does not say which render.json (old or candidate) the drift check then compares the live files against, after step 2 has already rewritten .romeu/bin and the workspace files, so the tool can report its own half-finished promotion as drift.
findings.scenario: romeu is killed after step 2, and the candidate dir is then damaged; the next command exits 4, and the preflight's drift check (01 1.5 step 3), comparing the old sbxenv.yaml against the render.json written in step 1, reports sbxenv.yaml as hand-edited, so the operator is told to run --overwrite-drift for an edit nobody made.
findings.change: In 01 1.6, have step 1 keep the previous file digests in render.json (previous) beside promoting, and say that when recovery cannot finish, romeu restores render.json to previous and reports interrupted-promotion-abandoned, never drift; add the case to the promotion fault injection of 10 10.1.
findings.cost: One field and two sentences.

findings.defect: 08 8.4 does not say what happens when the snapshot cannot be written (disk full, memory dir unmounted).
findings.scenario: The host disk is full; each post-commit fails to write heads.bundle; by 04 4.3 that stops the repo's own post-commit hooks too, and the failure lands in julieta state and a hook-failed event that names no repo, so the operator sees nothing until the sandbox dies with a snapshot days old.
findings.change: Add to 08 8.4: the commit is never undone; the previous bundle is kept; the failure is recorded with the repo in heads.json on the host side (disabled-style marker, L4-16); the repo's own hooks still run (julieta's snapshot failure does not stop the chain); and romeu status shows "snapshot failing since <T>".
findings.cost: A paragraph and a rule change in 04 4.3 hooks run.

findings.defect: retire moves and never deletes, salvage payloads accumulate in memory dirs (08 8.1 caps), and salvage refs accumulate, but nothing measures that growth and no Deferred decisions row names a cleanup.
findings.scenario: After a year the .attic and memory dirs hold tens of GiB; the host disk fills, and the next snapshot and salvage fail for lack of space (L4-22, L4-10); and if the salvage cap is per directory, later salvages go over-cap.
findings.change: Say in 08 8.1 whether the salvage cap is per salvage or per directory; add a doctor warning on the size of .attic and of each memory dir; add a Deferred decisions row "an explicit attic and payload cleanup command" reopened by the first doctor size warning.
findings.cost: A sentence, a doctor row, a deferred row.

findings.defect: After approve --toolchain, an sbx version that has no recording is accepted, and the spec does not say whether an sbx ls --json that fails to parse or lacks a field is an error, an absent sandbox or an unknown one.
findings.scenario: sbx renames the workspace path field; romeu parses an empty path and refuses every sandbox with RJ-203, or reads no sandbox at all and enters the absent rows of 01 1.6 (L4-3).
findings.change: In 10 10.3 and 04 4.1, state that an sbxdrv parser failure, a missing field, or an sbx version above the newest recorded one is a distinct error (exit 2, new id, "sbx output not understood") that no state transition may follow, and that gate 1 prints when the new sbx version has no recording.
findings.cost: One error id and two sentences.

findings.defect: doctor compares the derived files with render.json and the ledger view with its re-derivation, but not the project record with the facts sbx owns (generations against sbx ls, egressApplied against sbx policy ls), nor the salvage records with their refs.
findings.scenario: An sbx reset drops the per-sandbox allow rules; egressApplied still lists them; doctor passes, and the next install fails on a blocked host, which the operator then approves one-off in the native queue.
findings.change: Add doctor rows: each open generation has a sandbox in sbx ls and each sandbox has a generation; egressApplied equals what sbx policy ls reports per sandbox; the refs check of L4-11.
findings.cost: Two or three doctor rows that read sbx.

findings.defect: retire runs rm if needed but has no --accept-loss, and its --force both allows retiring a project still in the spec and skips the TTY confirmation of salvage-only work.
findings.scenario: A script runs retire --force to retire a project the spec still lists; it also skips the confirmation that would have listed two branches not on origin; and what retire does when its inner salvage is incomplete is unstated.
findings.change: Split retire --force into --in-spec and the confirmation (TTY only, or --accept-loss=<reasons> as in L4-13), and state that an incomplete inner salvage exits 5 before any move.
findings.cost: A flag and a sentence.

findings.defect: Block A measures no loss-relevant sbx fact except A6, so the salvage design rests on unmeasured behavior.
findings.scenario: On real sbx, sbx env exec on a stopped sandbox fails instead of starting it, and sbx env rm deletes the workload's per-name volumes; the J6 and J10 designs were never confronted with either before block B.
findings.change: Add a block A probe that records: exec on a stopped sandbox; sbx ls --json during a daemon restart and after an upgrade; sbx env rm and the workload's volumes; whether the sandbox daemon answers on a stopped sandbox; whether a stopped sandbox's disk can be read from the host. Name in its Settles cell 01 1.6, 08 8.5 and L4-3's absent rule.
findings.cost: One probe, maybe 15 minutes per host.

findings.defect: The fake sbx replays only recorded sessions, and block A records happy paths, so the failure rows of the generation machine cannot run in CI.
findings.scenario: The rows "sbx env run returns non-zero", "sandbox found absent" and a failed sandbox half are never exercised outside the host suite, and B3 has no journey for them.
findings.change: Add to 10 10.3 a rule that the probes record failure sessions too (an ls error, an exec timeout, a VM that will not start, an exec that hits a full disk), and that each generation row of 01 1.6 names the recorded session that exercises it.
findings.cost: Recorder cases and a mapping table.

findings.defect: Salvage branches are created under refs/heads/salvage/, where a later git push --all or --mirror publishes them with the untracked files they hold, each salvage adds more, and every later snapshot bundles all of them.
findings.scenario: After three salvages the agent runs git push --mirror; nine salvage branches with untracked .env-like files reach origin, and each snapshot now carries every past salvage.
findings.change: Create salvage refs under refs/salvage/<generation>/<salvage-id>/ (outside refs/heads), include them in the bundle explicitly, and exclude earlier generations' salvage refs from 08 8.4 snapshots.
findings.cost: A ref name change in 08 8.5, 03 3.11 and I17 cases.

findings.defect: Untracked non-ignored files are captured with no cap while ignored files have the 1 GiB cap, and a nested repository's dirty tree and stashes are not mentioned.
findings.scenario: An agent leaves a 6 GiB untracked model file; the salvage bundle grows to that size or the exec times out (L4-31); a nested repo with uncommitted work is bundled at its HEAD only and the result is complete.
findings.change: State in 08 8.5 step 2 that untracked files count against the same cap and are listed over-cap beyond it, and that nested repositories get the same dirty-tree and stash capture as top-level ones.
findings.cost: Two sentences and two container cases.

findings.defect: Every subprocess has a timeout (10 10.6), but the timeout of the salvage exec, which moves up to a GiB over virtiofs, and what a timeout leaves behind are unstated.
findings.scenario: A large salvage hits a default timeout; julieta is killed mid-write, the memory dir holds a partial salvage dir, and the generation stays salvaging (L4-6).
findings.change: Name the salvage exec timeout in 04 4.1 (scaled to the cap, or none with an interrupt), and state in 08 8.5 that a partial salvage dir is ignored by verification and kept.
findings.cost: One value and one sentence.

findings.defect: The default workload has per-name volumes that reattach on recreate, and the spec does not say what they hold, whether sbx env rm removes them, or whether salvage covers them.
findings.scenario: The workload keeps agent state in a volume; rm removes it and salvage never enumerated it, or recreate reattaches state from a generation that romeu has closed.
findings.change: Have probe A12 list the workload's volumes and their paths, and state in 08 8.5 whether each is salvaged, excluded as acknowledged loss, or outlives rm.
findings.cost: A probe observation and a sentence.

findings.defect: No journey shows how to restore a salvage record's dirty-tree commit, stash commits or ignored.tar.gz, and J6 step 4's "the operator fixes it" has no steps for fixing an unreadable or over-cap item from the host.
findings.scenario: After recreate the operator needs yesterday's uncommitted edits; J10 step 3 shows only a branch recovery, so they guess at refs and at untarring an archive the host is told never to extract from the memory dir (I24).
findings.change: Add to J6 (or a new journey) the restore steps: check out the salvage worktree commit into the new sandbox through a push from the host's salvage ref, apply stash-<n>, and where ignored.tar.gz is extracted (inside the sandbox, never on the host); spell out "fixes it" per reason.
findings.cost: A journey section and a guide page.

findings.defect: romeu stop runs julieta snapshot --all, then sbx stop, with no rule for a failed snapshot.
findings.scenario: The snapshot fails on a full disk; stop either stops anyway with a stale snapshot or exits and leaves the sandbox running, and the operator cannot tell which from the text.
findings.change: State that a failed snapshot is reported and stop goes on (the disk persists), with exit 1 after the stop.
findings.cost: One sentence.

findings.defect: No success criterion measures the objective's last line; it is reached only through S6 (I17 tag pairs) and S7 (J6 and J10 pass).
findings.scenario: v1.0.0 ships with every S green and no evidence that a kill at each step of rm converges, or that salvage is complete over a stated scope.
findings.change: Add an S12: "for each step of the destructive step list (01 1.6) a killed romeu converges, and salvage is complete over the scope of 00 0.1", with evidence the fault-injection test of L4-2 and the I17 cases.
findings.cost: A row and an acceptance item.

findings.defect: Q25 is marked decided and recorded in ADR 0008, yet stays in the Open questions table, whose own rule says a question leaves it when settled.
findings.scenario: A reader counting open questions before block A counts a closed one, and the rule "leaves this table when it is settled" is shown not to hold.
findings.change: Move Q25 out now, or amend the rule to "leaves this table in the task that writes its record" and name that task once.
findings.cost: A row removed or a sentence changed.

findings.defect: No row records a loss mechanism v1 leaves out (snapshot history, salvage of a non-starting sandbox, state outside the recorded repos, a host-visible last-good-snapshot signal, host state migration), although the index says a deferral without a row is an oversight and ADR 0005 says what a later step depends on is never deferred; and the successes row's cost cell omits that the host cannot learn the last good snapshot time.
findings.scenario: v1 ships without these, and nothing reopens them before the first loss, because they were never written down as deferred.
findings.change: For each mechanism not built after L4-9, L4-10, L4-16 and L4-19, add a row with what holds (the narrower guarantee) and an observable trigger (the first salvage record with reason sandbox-half-failed, the first --from-host whose facts show dirty work); add the snapshot-time cost to the successes row.
findings.cost: Up to five rows and one cell.

findings.defect: Two rows share one trigger (rotation of the ledger and tuning its starting values, both reopened by doctor's size warning), and the finding-class row is reopened only once another deferred row's mechanism exists.
findings.scenario: doctor's size warning fires and two rows reopen for one decision; the finding-class row can never fire while the gate-run row stays deferred.
findings.change: Merge the two ledger rows, or give tuning a trigger of its own (ingest reporting a cap reached); write the finding-class trigger so it is observable on its own or mark it as dependent on the named row.
findings.cost: Two cells.

postmortem: Months after v1.0.0 the operator stops trusting the product. (1) The promise was bigger than the mechanism: a repo cloned into $HOME/scratch and a local database were sandbox-only, rm said complete (00 0.1, 0.5; 08 8.5; 03 3.11; 06 6.2). (2) The VM disk filled; salvage writes into the sandbox repo and failed; --from-host has no dirty trees or stashes, and the facts file saying dirty 14, stashes 2 was never shown (08 8.5, 04 4.2, 03 3.10, J10). (3) A reset --hard plus a commit rewrote the one heads.bundle, and the reflog is never salvaged (08 8.4, 03 3.11). (4) The sandbox died mid-snapshot; the temp leftover made the J10 run refuse with exit 2 (08 8.1, 01 1.6). (5) After an sbx upgrade, salvage exited 3 until gate 1; a hand fix made it exit 4 (01 1.5, I7, T074). (6) sbx restarted, one ls came back empty, run closed the generation as lost and created a same-name sandbox without asking (01 1.6, J10). (7) Kills were tested only in the promotion commit; an rm killed after sbx env rm recorded a good salvage as lost, and a failed sandbox half left a generation that run and adopt each refused (10 10.1, I17, 10 10.3, 01 1.6). (8) Re-cloning a navigation clone took three salvages with it, unnoticed; thin bundle bases were force-pushed away and collected (02 2.3, 2.6, I6, 03 3.6). (9) Origin was not the safe copy 05 5.4 said; ADR 0008 had written that the token deletes branches. (10) --accept-loss needed no TTY; husky disabled snapshots for weeks, visible only inside a live sandbox; and the ledger got a hostile-input table, races, a full-disk row and a crash rule (13) while the part holding a week of work got a paragraph (04 4.2, 08 8.4, 02 2.5, index: Deferred decisions).
lens_critique: This lens treats every byte in a sandbox as work and every loss as a defect, but for this product the agent is expected to be wrong and disposable, and much sandbox state (caches, scratch, transcripts with echoed tokens) is better lost than kept; a salvage that keeps everything also widens what reaches the host and what a hostile agent can plant there. The lens also undervalues push-early as the real defense: most of its findings shrink if the product makes pushing cheap and visible rather than salvage complete. And it judges completeness by what can go wrong on one machine, while the product's own premise (S3, J12) is that sandboxes are recreated freely.
missing_viewpoint: No lens speaks for the agent's adversary within the operator's own accounts, the person who reviews and merges what agents push to GitHub and has to recover from a bad merge or a deleted branch there; recovery on the remote (origin, rulesets, the operator's token) falls between L2, L4 and L7.
